title: [2026.10.23] Patch Notes: Charged Jet Stream and Glowing Arrows
text:
New: Charged Jet Stream
• Jet Stream now takes 2 seconds to cast, and nothing shortens it.
• Press a movement key during the cast to loose it early: let go at once for 30% damage, wait the full 2 seconds for 150%.
• Its arrow now carries a water slash, leaves a trail of dust, and lights the ground as it flies.

Combat
• The bow cast pose now raises and draws the bow slowly across the whole cast.
• The bow's cast glow now stays at your side whichever way you turn.
• Dashes show fire footprints again, alongside the earth trail.

title: [2026.10.21] Patch Notes: The Bow's Skills, Teleport Effect and Door Circles
text:
New: The Bow's Skills
• The Bow now has its own 22 skills in the Passing Cloud style of Celestia, the Wandering Sky: 3 ultimates, 11 actives and 8 passives.
• Cloudburst: a rain cloud follows you and drops arrows on everything near you, faster the faster you attack.
• Wandering Sky: hard to hit and fast until a blow lands, and every attack you dodge is answered with an arrow.
• Thunderhead: one heavy shot that grows with how far your accuracy goes past a sure hit.
• Updraft dashes you to the spot you click, and Rainbow lobs an arrow in a real arc onto the spot you aim.
• Bow arrows are now real arrows in flight, and every Bow skill has its own picture and effect.

Combat
• Multi-hit skills now work out their damage once per target and show it as their hits one after another, Ragnarok-style.
• No mix of slows can drop anyone below 30% of their speed. The stats window shows your movement speed and its limits.
• While you attack, your character keeps facing the target even if you walk or open a window.
• A skill aimed at a creature now shows its effects on that creature on every screen.

New: Teleport Effect
• Fly Wing, Butterfly Wing, doors, the GM travel command and entering the world now share one teleport: a burst of light and a sound where you stand, a fade to black, and the same burst as you appear.
• The fade takes one second each way, and the trip only starts once the screen is black.
• While you are away you cannot move, attack, cast or use items, and everything on you — glows, auras, your name plate — is hidden.
• Other players see you vanish and appear too.

Map & Travel
• Doors are now glowing circles on the ground, still coloured by where they lead: yellow for towns, green for fields, purple for dungeons.
• A door takes you only when you stand on its circle — jumping over it does nothing.

title: [2026.10.20] Patch Notes: Tainted and Blighted Creatures, Tougher Dungeons and Level-Matched Gear
text:
New: Tainted and Blighted Creatures
• Every creature now has a Tainted and a Blighted version. They live in the dungeons: Tainted on the first and middle floors, Blighted on the deepest floors beside the elite.
• A few Tainted creatures also roam the ordinary fields. The newbie fields stay easy.
• Elites now call Tainted and Blighted creatures to their side.
• Harder creatures wear a dark glow that grows stronger with their toughness. The toughest creatures trail rising smoke.

Creatures and Combat
• Every creature wears gear that fits its level, so a creature far above you is a real fight.
• Health for players and creatures now grows with level: a creature of your level takes about 5 ordinary hits.
• Tougher creatures pay more in experience and drops, and the rarest Salts, Inks and materials drop only from them.

Items & Crafting
• Quench Oil drops less often, to match how much Temper Dust a climb uses.
• Each Tainted and Blighted creature drops its own rarer version of its material.

title: [2026.10.19] Patch Notes: Real-World Clock, Dark Mode, Skill Icons, New Art and Sign-In Fix
text:
New: The World Runs on Real Time
• The world's clock is now the real time in the Philippines (GMT+8). Day runs from 6 AM to 6 PM and night from 6 PM to 6 AM, so evening play is at night.
• The date is today's real date, and the season follows the month: winter Dec–Feb, spring Mar–May, summer Jun–Aug, autumn Sep–Nov.
• The plate under the minimap now shows the time in big digital numbers, with the date and today's weather below it.
• The Calendar shows a whole month at a time, Sunday to Saturday, with each day's weather. Use the arrows to move between months.

New: Dark Mode
• The game's look is now dark. Every window, button, tooltip, the chat, the minimap, the date under it and the Calendar are drawn dark, with all text kept readable.
• The item card you open with a right-click is dark too, including the picture panel and the card-slot strip.
• Item pictures in your bag, your worn gear and the hotbar keep their true colours in dark mode.

Costumes
• Wearing a costume such as the Adventurer Outfit no longer leaves see-through holes in the body at the neck, wrists or waist from some camera angles.

Skills
• Every skill in the Skills window now shows its own picture. Skills with no points in them show it in grey, and skills your weapon mastery hasn't reached yet are grey and faint.

Gear Looks
• The lightning around a graded armour set now spreads further out from the body.
• Ice, water and dark weapon effects no longer hide the weapon in your bag, gear, hotbar and tooltips.

Sign-In
• Going back to character select after a long time in the world no longer asks you to sign in again.

New Art
• Three new pictures of Veyra and Morwen now appear behind the sign-in screen and on the loading screen.
• On the website, the Sword and Scythe in the Fourteen Kashira showcase now show Veyra and Morwen, and the Media page has a gallery of all the game's artwork.

title: [2026.10.18] Patch Notes: Power Limits, Summoned Bosses, Card Slots and Creature Aggro
text:
New: Every Kind of Power Has a Limit
• Your level, every stat, the Ring, gear grades and folds, Ink and card slots all stop at a ceiling, so a new player can always catch up. The Character window shows each limit beside its number.
• The Ring stops at level 99: 99 points, and each Ring stat takes up to 33 ranks at +1% each. Defense gives +1 hard defence per rank.

New: Summoned Bosses
• Blood Ronin, Frost Ronin, Wraithmother, Inferno Mask and the fourteen shadows no longer roam. Each has a Summoner standing where it lives — bring the materials other elites drop and call it out for everyone nearby to fight.
• The four great elites change weapon, armour and fighting style every time they return.
• Fourteen elites now guard the world, one for every weapon, spread across fields and the deepest dungeon floors.

Combat
• Defence comes in two parts: hard defence takes a percentage off every hit (up to 90%), then soft defence from VIT takes a flat amount. A critical hit ignores both.
• Chance to hit is now HIT + 80 − FLEE. HIT is level and DEX, FLEE is level and AGI, and every creature on you past the second takes 10% off your FLEE.
• LUK now gives perfect dodge: 0.1% of ordinary attacks miss you outright, even critical ones.
• Critical hits deal double damage, up to triple, and crit chance can reach 100%.
• Attack speed is shown as ASPD, up to 190 — five attacks a second.
• Guard Stance, Bulwark, Squall and Ember Bolt now raise or lower defence instead of cutting damage.
• A creature chases you until you have been outside its aggro area for 5 seconds, then stops where it stands — it no longer walks home, and it always fights back when hit.
• Hit by someone new, a creature turns to them only once they have done it more damage than the one it is fighting.
• Gentle creatures — Plopling, Flutterby, Squeak, Capling, Mossnail, Hootie, Gillie, Newtie, Pando, Mudpup, Burrowbo, Pilfer, Wyrmlet, Dewdrop, Emberwyrm and Willo — never attack first.

Items & Gear
• Gear no longer has rarity. A piece is worth its grade, its folds, its Ink and its card slots.
• Weapons can hold up to 4 card slots and armour up to 2; a piece's name ends with its slot count. Add slots at the Smith's new Slot tab.
• Monsters drop an exact copy of what they wear, folds, Ink and slots included. Stronger monsters wear better gear.
• Recycling gives back half of everything a piece is worth, and shops pay for gear by that same worth.
• Ink lines now grow with the grade of the piece they are written on.

Characters
• Every character has been reset for this update. Your account is kept.

title: [2026.10.17] Patch Notes: One Smith for All Gear, Blocked Dashes and Ink Info
text:
Crafting
• Gunnar the Smith now works every piece: metal, cloth and leather. Odette the Weaver and Rook the Tanner have left Lastline.
• On the Ink tab, hover the i beside your Ink's name to see every stat it can write and how much. A stat already in another slot is greyed.

Combat
• A dash that runs into a wall, a creature or anything else now stops right there, and its strike misses.
• Piercing Gust's follow-up lunges only fire with a sword in hand. Switch away and back, and the charges left still work.
• Crossed Branches charges no longer lengthen your sword. A basic attack lunges at a target within Piercing Gust's range; if the lunge is blocked, you walk in and swing as normal.
• Crossed Branches now has a single level. Points spent past it are given back.

Town
• The Hatter now wears a top hat.

title: [2026.10.16] Patch Notes: A Gentler Start, Hats with Effects, Weapon Enchants, Armour Auras and Batch Recycling
text:
New: A Gentler Start
• New characters start in a +5 Chainmail, Iron Sabatons and Chain Mantle, with a +0 Sword, and carry 100 Newbie Potions.
• Newbie Potions heal 80 to 100 at once and weigh nothing. They cannot be dropped, sold, stored or traded.
• Every Healing Potion now heals a range, rolled each drink, and heals more for the same price: a Minor Healing Potion heals 130 to 170, up to 2,800 to 3,600 for a Grand.
• Lastline Field 1 and Parley Field 1 now hold only creatures in plain, unfolded gear: a new player in the starting armour survives at least five blows from any of them. Gloop King no longer lives there.
• Everyone, players and creatures, has more health at every level.
• "Your First Gear" now teaches folding on your Sword alone: fold it to +5, free the first time.

Creatures & Drops
• Every creature now drops one material of its own, and how rare it is follows the creature's gear: plain gear drops a Common, and each grade up a rarer one, up to Legendary.
• Rarer materials sell for much more, so every kind of hunt pays about the same on average.
• Elites always drop a Rare or better: two Rare from a grade D elite every kill, a chance at an Epic or a Legendary from the stronger ones.
• A rescued character hands over its creature's material in its real rarity: a few Commons, or a chance at a rarer piece.
• Creatures no longer wear helmets, and the Iron Helm, Leather Cap and Padded Hood are gone from the game. Anyone holding one, or a material that was removed, is paid its old shop price.

New: Hats
• All fifteen hats now give stats and one effect while worn: a chance to poison, burn, stun or silence, stacking speed or crit, mana or health over time, a burst when you draw your weapon, and more. Each hat's card says what it does.
• Every hat works with any weapon, and each one suits a way of fighting. Try them and find yours.
• A hat is the same on every copy: it never rolls, folds or takes a rarity.
• The Chef's Hat gives +15% experience from every kill.
• For beta testing, the Hatter by the fountain in the middle of Lastline sells every hat for 1u.

Crafting
• Recycling now gives back half of every fold and quench a piece ever took, Raw folds included, and never less than 1 Temper Dust: a Raw piece straight from a creature is no longer worth nothing.
• Tick as many carried pieces as you like on a station's Recycle page and recycle them all with one press. Worn pieces are recycled one at a time.
• Graded weapons carry an enchant of their kind: fire, water, ice, nature or dark streams off the weapon, stronger at higher grades, drawn or put away. It shows from every angle.
• A full graded armour set (body, garment and shoes) raises a lightning aura around you at the grade of its lowest piece: a cloud first, then lightning from grade C.
• Graded items' pictures glow sky blue everywhere but their card.
• Behind a wall, only your body shows blue: your weapon's enchant and your armour's aura no longer turn into blue shapes.
• The Fold and Quench pages show how much Temper Dust or Quench Oil and Unsigned you carry.

Combat
• The Shuriken now plays its take-out and put-away, instead of jumping between your back and your hand, and stands and walks in its own poses.
• A dash skill's damage, Piercing Gust's included, now lands when you arrive, not as you set off.
• Auto-combat starts with auto-loot taking everything, a healing potion at 70% health and Free Roam. Pressing Start closes every open window.

Map & Travel
• While a path shows, a pin stands on the ground where it leads, and the left of the screen names the map and how many metres are left.

Items & Shops
• Long item names in a shop no longer run into the quantity and price.
• "Don't ask quantity" now only skips the box when selling; buying always asks.
• The amount in the how-many box is selected, ready to type over.
• Moving a stack from the cart back to the dealer asks how many.
• Esc closes an item's card.
• Hovering a stack on the hotbar shows how many you carry.
• The stacking messages on screen are bolder.

title: [2026.10.15] Patch Notes: Item Pictures, Ragnarok Item Cards, Thrown Loot and a New Death
text:
New: Character Creation
• Head and Body are now two tabs. Head holds your hair colour and its arrows change the hairstyle; Body holds your outfit colours and its arrows change the body.
• Opening the Head tab zooms the preview in on the head, so you can see the hairstyle up close.
• Colours are remembered per body and per hairstyle while you create: paint one, look at others, and it is still painted when you come back.
• The character preview is drawn with fewer ink lines inside the body; its outline stays.

Login Screen
• The login and character screens now show a painted town behind them, with the unwritten title across the top.

Combat
• Falling in battle now plays a new death animation.
• Your weapon slips out of your hand as you fall: it bounces, spins and comes to rest on the ground beside you until you return. It stays in your bag the whole time.
• Creatures holding weapons drop theirs the same way.
• The "Return to last saved point" window now appears once the fall has finished, not the moment you are hit.

New: Item Pictures
• Every item now has its own picture. Bag, worn gear, storage, crafting and hotbar boxes show the picture on a square in the item's rarity colour.
• Hover an item to see its full name. Right-click any item, in a box, in the shop or named in chat, to open its item card.
• The item card is a larger picture with the details beside it: drag its title bar to move it, scroll long details, and see its card slots along the bottom.
• Monster materials show as a box in the colour of their rarity.

Loot
• Drops now lie on the ground as their picture, and every drop is thrown there: it flies out of whatever dropped it, spins, and bounces where it lands. The sparkle is gone.
• Whenever something arrives in your bag, a small card pops up at the top of the screen with its picture and name.

Interface
• The target panel at the top of the screen is gone.

title: [2026.10.14] Patch Notes: Folding and Quenching Reworked, Shop Cart and Tax, Weapon Swing Speeds
text:
New: Folding and Quenching
• Every piece of gear now has a base value, so a fresh Raw +0 drop is worth wearing. Each dropped piece rolls its base from 85% to 115%, shown on its card as "Base 54 (108%)".
• Every grade now folds to +10, and every fold and every quench adds to the piece for good. A higher grade at +0 is always stronger than the grade below it at +10.
• Folds up to +4 always work. From +4 a fold can fail and drops the piece back one fold, never below +4.
• A quench at +10 either raises the piece one grade or fails. Without Salt a failure drops it one grade; Coarse Salt keeps its grade at +4, Fine also raises the chance, and Pure keeps it at +9.
• Rarity now multiplies the whole piece. Fine Salt is now Epic and Pure Salt Legendary, and both can drop from any creature. Merging takes 20 Coarse for a Fine and 5 Fine for a Pure.
• Station fees and the Keeper's teleport now grow with level: a teleport costs 40u a door for each of your levels.
• Every character was reset for this change.

New: The Shop Cart
• The Tool Dealer is now one window: For sale, your Cart, and your Inventory side by side. Every row shows its price.
• Drag or double-click items into the cart to buy or sell, then press Confirm to do it all at once. The cart shows what you pay or get before you confirm.
• Every item now has one value. The shop adds a 33% Tax when it sells to you and takes it when it buys from you. Selling pays exactly what it did before.
• Fly Wing and the minor potions now cost 51u, Healing Potion and Mana Draught 224u. Everything else costs the same.
• Buying something back costs what you were paid plus Tax. Every sale is kept as its own buy-back.

New: The Smith Window
• The smith, loom and tannery window now has tabs: Fold, Quench, Ink and Recycle, over a grid of your gear.
• Pick a piece to see what the work costs, and what one more fold adds to its stats, then press the one button at the bottom.
• Salt is now a checkbox, and each Ink slot shows the stat written in it.

Interface
• The currency is now called Unsigned, shown as "u".
• Item cards group the piece's own stats in bold, then its written stats, then its trademark and cards. A trademark line now names its skill.
• Short messages now stack at the top middle of the screen: green when something is done, red when it is refused, yellow for warnings.
• Dragging an item or a skill now shows a see-through copy of it.
• The "how many?" box now has Confirm and Cancel.

Combat
• Every weapon now has its own swing speed. Daggers and fists are the fastest at 0.8 seconds a swing, swords and wands take 1 second, and a sniper is the slowest at 1.4 seconds.
• Bare hands swing once a second. Before, everything swung every 0.6 seconds, so fights are slower.
• AGI, DEX, your ring, leather armour and buffs speed your swings up exactly as before.

Movement
• Shoes no longer give movement speed. Only buffs and slows change how fast you move.
• Walking, running and sprinting are a little slower than before.
• The camera no longer zooms out as far: the furthest view is two thirds of what it was.

Monsters
• Every monster now moves at its own speed. Slimes, snails and mushrooms are slow; mice, bats and raccoons are fast.
• Shootling and Canewick never move. They shoot from where they stand, and cannot be pushed or pulled.
• Shootling now carries a Sniper.
• Flutterby and Crawlet wear weaker gear and are easier to fight.
• Flutterby Scale Dust and Crawlet Cocoon no longer drop.

title: [2026.10.13] Patch Notes: Gear Drops and Creature Materials
text:
New: Gear Drops
• Gear is no longer forged. Every creature can drop a piece of what it wears: its weapon, or its head, body, shoes or garment piece.
• A dropped piece comes with a rarity. Ordinary creatures drop Common, Uncommon and Rare pieces, elites drop Epic ones, and shadows drop Legendary ones.
• The rarer a piece is, the more every fold on it is worth.
• Every weapon is wielded by ordinary creatures, by an elite and by one shadow, and every shadow now wears a full set of armour.

New: Creature Materials
• Creatures no longer drop gold. Every creature now drops a material that only it has; sell it at any shop.
• Some creatures also carry a second, rarer material with a coloured name, from Uncommon up to Legendary.
• An elite drops its material in several piles on every kill, and nothing an elite drops is picked up automatically.

Crafting
• Folding now takes Temper Dust and quenching takes Quench Oil, whatever the piece is made of. The old metals, cloths and leathers are gone.
• Every creature drops Temper Dust and Quench Oil. Harder creatures drop more.
• Recycling a piece gives back half the Temper Dust, Quench Oil and gold its folds and quenches took. Folds made at Raw give nothing back.
• The smith, the loom and the tannery fold, quench, ink and recycle. They no longer make gear.

Items & Shops
• Healing Potions and Mana Draughts now come in five sizes each: Minor, plain, Greater, Superior and Grand. The Tool Dealer sells all ten.
• Potions, Fly Wings, Butterfly Wings and Antidotes are bought from the Tool Dealer and no longer drop from creatures.
• Each creature now drops one find of its own, by its element: Fire, Water, Earth and Wind creatures drop their element's converters, and the others drop a food.
• Foods now last 5 minutes. New food: Sage Stew, which raises magic attack.
• Shops no longer buy foods or converters, and pay far less for gear, Ink and Salt.
• Your purse can now hold far more gold.

Combat
• Every creature and elite now wears a full set of gear and a weapon, and its stats are built for that weapon.
• A creature's gear decides how hard it is, whatever its level: the rarer the thing it drops and the harder it is to find, the better its gear.
• Better-geared creatures pay more experience, and their materials sell for more.
• When several players fight one creature, the one who did the most owns its loot, and the experience is shared by what each did: damage, being chased, healing others, the first hit and the last.

New Characters
• A new character starts wearing a Sword, a Chainmail and Iron Sabatons, and the first tutorial teaches folding them.
• All characters and stored items were reset for this update.

Saved Characters
• Saving a character that never fights now pays gold and some of its creature's material.

title: [2026.10.12] Patch Notes: Auto-Combat, the Keeper and the New Bag
text:
New: the Bag
• Your bag is now a grid of boxes, like the hotbar: each item by its name, a stack with its count. A tab shows all 24 of its boxes, so you can see how full it is.
• Sort by Name, Held or Rarity; with no sort chosen, things stay in the order they arrived, newest at the end.
• Double-click to use, wear or merge. Drag a box onto another to swap them, onto the hotbar, or out of the window to drop it. The right-click menu is gone.
• What you wear now has its own frame beside the bag: the camera turns to your character and stands you in it, wearing your real gear. Drag gear into the frame to put it on; the right slot lights up while you drag.
• Taking gear off needs a free box in your Equip tab.

New: the Keeper
• A new NPC in every town: saves your return point, opens your Storage, and teleports you between towns.
• Storage is a grid, beside your bag. Double-click moves all of a stack; Ctrl + double-click moves one; or drag between the two.
• Butterfly Wing (back to your save point) and Fly Wing (a random spot on the map you are on) are now in the game.

New: Auto-Combat
• Press T (or open System ▸ Auto-Combat) and your character hunts on its own — choose Standing, Radius or Free Roam.
• Auto-Skills: pick up to four skills to cast automatically, even ones not on your hotbar.
• Auto-Potion: drinks a health or mana potion when you fall below the percentage you set.
• Auto-Loot with a loot filter: choose which kinds of items go straight to your bag, and the rarest drop chance worth taking.

Chat
• Shift-click any item to put it in your chat line. Send it, and anyone can point at it to see its tooltip, in every kind of chat, private messages included.

Interface
• The chosen tab in every window is now filled in, so it stands out.
• Floating text has its black outline again: damage numbers, names, the kill combo, zone titles and battle notices.
• That outline is now solid black, so floating text reads over any ground.

Items & Shops
• Fixed: with more than 40 different items, the newest ones no longer go missing from the All tab.
• Each bag tab (Equip, Use, Material, Etc) now holds up to 24 entries. A stack counts as one, and what you wear counts in Equip.
• You can carry up to 2000 weight, plus 30 for every point of STR. What you wear counts too.
• When a tab is full or something is too heavy, it stays on the ground (or in the shop) and the chat tells you why. Taking a pile out of storage takes as many as you can carry.
• Quest rewards always arrive, even past your limits — the chat tells you when your bag is over.
• The bag shows how full the open tab is, and your weight against your limit.
• Item names are now coloured by rarity.
• Shops now have Buyback — get back what you sold by mistake.
• Folding and Quenching now work on gear you're wearing.
• Used-up consumables stay on your hotbar, shown in red, ready for when you restock.

Combat
• New kill combo: chain kills to raise your combo, and every combo step increases the EXP and zeny you earn.
• New EXP per hour and zeny per hour counters.
• New Combat Log tab in the chat window.
• Mobs no longer vanish in tall grass: once a mob has attacked you, or you've damaged it, it shows as a blue shape through grass and anything else in the way.

Map & Travel
• The zone view now labels every portal with where it leads — click one to jump the view to that zone.
• Click any spot on the map to draw a guide on the ground leading there, even across zones.
• The zone view's mob list now shows how many of each mob are in the zone.
• The zone name now flashes on every map change, in the colour of its map type.
• Invisible walls now close off the edges and corners of every zone, so you can no longer step off the world.
• Dungeons are no longer boxed in by generated walls.

title: A new launcher
text: The launcher has a new look and now keeps itself up to date. If you already have the game, open your launcher as usual and press Start once: instead of the game, a small window downloads the new launcher (about 100 MB), which opens by itself and keeps your game without downloading it again. If your launcher says "Access to the path … is denied", download it again from the website. The Uninstall button in the new launcher removes the game from your computer.

title: Every weapon in 3D
text: The weapons are now 3D models held in your character's hands. The greatsword, warhammer, spear, bow, dagger, katar, staff, wand, sword, axe, shuriken, scythe and sniper each have their own model and their own way of being held, and each has its own place on your body when it is put away.

title: Choose your hair
text: Character creation has a new Hair picker: step through 13 hairstyles, or pick no hair. When your character has hair, the Colours row gains one more swatch, and you paint the hair any colour with the same picker you use for the clothes.

title: Headgear you can see
text: A hat, helmet or hood worn in the Head slot now shows on your 3D character with its real shape, and every other player sees it too. Full helmets and the hood hide your hair. Other hats cover it where they sit, so only the hair hanging below shows, and headbands leave it whole.

title: Quests arrive
text: Open the Quests window with J: Tutorial, Main Story and Side Quests. New characters are given "Your First Gear", where Gunnar the Smith walks you through forging, folding and wearing your first sword, chainmail and sabatons. Torvald, the off-duty raider who wanders Lastline, has a side quest: defeat 10 Ploplings in the field west of town. Follow a quest and arrows on the ground lead you to its next step, and the route shows on your minimap and in the new Map window (M).

title: Fenwick opens his shop
text: Fenwick the Tool Dealer in Lastline sells healing potions and antidotes, one or ten at a time, and buys anything that has a sell value. Your gold finally has somewhere to go.

title: A three-row hotbar
text: The hotbar is now 3 rows of 9: F1 to F9, 1 to 9, and a third row on keys you choose in Settings. Any slot can hold a skill, an item or a piece of gear. Every ultimate now waits 40 seconds after any ultimate is cast, on top of its own cooldown.

title: Skills are bought with mastery points
text: Every weapon mastery level gives you one mastery point. Spend points in the Skills window (K) to learn a skill and raise its level, up to 10, 5 or 1 depending on the skill. Each level after the first adds 5% to the skill's numbers. Characters made before this change get all their points back to spend.

title: Saved characters
text: Beat a normal monster or an elite and there is a 15% chance it turns back into a character for 30 seconds. One that never fights pays you gold, an ally fights at your side, and a rebel fights everyone and drops better loot. Monsters no longer drop gold when they die.

title: The launcher
text: The game now comes with a launcher. It downloads the whole game the first time, then only the files that changed, and starts the game when you press Start.

title: Hills, cliffs and rain that pools
text: The fields rise and fall in hills, with rock cliffs along some roads and slopes up onto the high ground. When it rains, puddles form on level ground and lakes fill the hollows and spill downhill, the same for every player on the map.

title: A whole world
text: The world is now three regions: 75 maps plus Lastline, with cities, towns, fields and dungeon floors, and every place has a name.

title: Forging, elites and shadows
text: Make your own gear: forge it, fold it, quench it for a better grade, write stats on it with Ink, or take it apart for half of what went into it. Monsters are now normals, elites and shadows, and each of the fourteen shadows calls an elite to its side.
